summary: Configured >=512MB compressed zram swap on node1 via an Ansible playbook run from node2 (the control node with ansible-core installed). The swap is active at boot (generator-managed unit wired into swap.target) and preferred over disk swap via a higher priority (100 vs -2). Both node1 and node2 were restarted per the evidence protocol, each showing a changed boot identity and full recovery.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 (RHEL 10, existing disk swap /dev/vda3 2G priority -2) and node2 (Ubuntu 24.04, ansible-core 2.20 pre-installed) to identify node2 as the Ansible control node
Wired passwordless root SSH from node2 to node1 using the cluster-provided CLUSTER_SSH_PUBKEY/CLUSTER_SSH_PRIVKEY keypair
Created Ansible inventory and playbook on node2 (/root/ansible-zram/) targeting node1

Playbook installs zram-generator package, writes /etc/systemd/zram-generator.conf with zram-size = max(ram/2, 512) (yields ~980MB, exceeds 512MB minimum), compression-algorithm = zstd, swap-priority = 100 (beats disk swap's -2)
Ran playbook: installed package, wrote config, activated /dev/zram0 as swap at priority 100 with zstd compression; verified via swapon --show and /sys/block/zram0/comp_algorithm
Confirmed dev-zram0.swap is generator-managed and auto-wired into swap.target every boot from the config file -- no manual systemctl enable needed

Captured healthy baselines (boot_id, uptime, swap state) on both nodes, then restarted node1 via async systemctl reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed new boot_id and zram0 swap auto-active post-boot (980M/zstd/priority 100)
Restarted node2 similarly, confirmed new boot_id, then re-ran the playbook from node2 against node1 to prove full Ansible control-path recovery (idempotent run, changed=0, swap state intact)

evidence.requirement: node1 has >=512MB compressed in-memory (zram) swap configured via Ansible
evidence.summary: zram-generator package availability confirmed, playbook written defining zram-size=max(ram/2,512) with zstd compression, playbook run shows /dev/zram0 activated at 980M (>512MB)

evidence.requirement: zram swap is preferred over disk-backed swap
evidence.summary: swapon --show shows /dev/zram0 at priority 100 vs /dev/vda3 disk swap at priority -2, both before and after node1 restart
/sys/block/zram0/comp_algorithm shows zstd selected, confirmed both immediately after configuration and after reboot

evidence.requirement: zram swap is active at boot (persists across restart)
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id d9f8550d captured, reboot issued, node1 came back with new boot_id 5d081df6 and new uptime, with zram0 swap automatically active at 980M/zstd/priority 100 without any manual intervention

evidence.requirement: node1 restart evidence: healthy baseline -> restart -> changed boot identity -> recovered state
evidence.summary: node1 baseline boot_id/uptime/swap captured, reboot acknowledged before disconnect, polled through connection drop until reachable, new boot_id and uptime confirmed, swap and zram config verified healthy post-boot

evidence.requirement: node2 restart evidence: healthy baseline -> restart -> changed boot identity -> recovered state
evidence.summary: node2 baseline boot_id captured, reboot acknowledged before disconnect, polled through connection drop until reachable, new boot_id confirmed, then Ansible control-plane functionality (SSH to node1, playbook run) verified fully recovered with idempotent zero-change result
